risk_title: Escalating cross-border insecurity linked to the Sudan conflict increases protection risks and humanitarian needs in eastern Chad
headline: Panel broadly agrees with ACAPS's High rating; sustained cross-border attacks seen as most likely
summary_text: Most of the Chad panel agrees with the High probability and impact 4 rating, with a minority seeing it as too low. Experts flag refugee–host tensions over water and health risks in overcrowded sites as gaps in the current analysis.

forecasts.text: Will cross-border attacks become sustained and recurrent, affecting multiple border localities in eastern Chad and causing significant civilian casualties, displacement or humanitarian access disruptions, before 6 May 2027?
Will attacks directly target strategic infrastructure in Chad (airports, military facilities, border posts or major transport corridors), causing significant disruption, before 6 May 2027?

Will armed groups, militias or proxy actors operating across the Chad–Sudan border become actively involved in cross-border hostilities, causing sustained violence, retaliatory attacks or territorial insecurity in eastern Chad, before 6 May 2027?
